input_packet.case_brief: Choose first moves after seeing a partner's suspicious activity while preserving legal safety, evidence integrity, and personal safety. action_planning
input_packet.anchor_visible_candidate:
Do not confront the partner, investigate privately, access systems unusually, or pick a reporting channel yourself. Tonight, write down exactly what you saw, preserve your own notes, tell your spouse in broad strokes, and contact two or three whistleblower attorneys.

Your first move is independent counsel first, not GC-first by default and not a self-chosen audit committee or external report. Let counsel review the facts and decide whether GC, the audit committee, regulators, or another path is safest. During intake, ask practical questions that test whether the attorney has a reflexive channel preference: when have they advised internal-first, audit-committee-first, or external-first, and why?

Attend Wednesday normally and avoid anything that looks like a sudden change in behavior. If the partner raises the encounter, keep the response narrow: do not deny, elaborate, confront, investigate, or be alone with the partner if avoidable. This is high risk, so do not let fear push you into filing before evidence review, but do not let fear make you do nothing either. Get counsel involved quickly and keep the first moves reversible.
input_packet.deck_pressure_candidate: Do not confront your partner, investigate on your own, access any systems unusually, or pick a reporting channel yourself. Tonight, write down exactly what you saw and preserve your own notes. Tell your spouse only in broad strokes. Contact two or three independent whistleblower attorneys as your next move. Let them review the facts first and decide whether any internal or external reporting path is safest. During intake, ask each attorney how they decide among internal, audit committee, or external channels so you can check for any built‑in bias. Attend Wednesday normally without abrupt changes in behavior. If your partner raises the encounter, keep your response minimal, avoid elaboration, and avoid being alone with them if you can. Move quickly but keep all early steps reversible until counsel guides you.
